title: Sampling and aliasing
summary: A tide gauge's water levels as a sampled signal: the tidal constituents it contains, the sampling theorem that says which of them a sampling rate can see, and the aliasing and filtering that follow.

concepts.label: Tide
concepts.description: The periodic rise and fall of sea level from the Moon's and Sun's gravity.

facts.text: Station 9414290, San Francisco, has recorded water levels since 1854.

children.label: Tidal constituent
children.description: One sinusoid of the tide with a fixed astronomical speed (M2, S2, N2, K1, O1).

children.label: Spring–neap cycle
children.description: The 14.77-day beat of M2 and S2: real, and close in period to the daily-sampling alias of M2.

children.label: Harmonic prediction
children.description: NOAA's predicted tide from the station's constituents (product=predictions): the expected signal to compare with.

concepts.label: Sampling
concepts.description: Reading a continuous signal at discrete times.

children.label: Nyquist frequency
children.description: Half the sampling rate: the highest frequency a sampler can represent.

children.label: Aliasing
children.description: A frequency above Nyquist reappearing at |f − k·fs|.

children.label: Anti-aliasing filter
children.description: A low-pass filter before the sampler; here the daily mean.

concepts.label: Spectrum
concepts.description: Amplitude per frequency, from a discrete Fourier transform.

children.label: Spectral leakage
children.description: Energy of a line spreading to neighbouring frequencies when the record is finite and unwindowed.
